observations: Two consoles are shown side-by-side: a PS4 Fat (left) and a PS4 Pro (right).
The PS4 Pro has the characteristic three-tier design.
The PS4 Fat has a two-tier design with a glossy and matte split top.
The 'SONY' logo is visible on the top tier of the Pro console in photo 1.
The 'PS4' logo is visible on the bottom tier edge of the Pro console in photo 1.
Both consoles appear dusty with visible fingerprints and smudge marks.
The background shows a retail environment with shelves of mobile phone boxes.
A banner for 'McSteve Online Gadget Store' is visible at the bottom.
No controllers, cables, or receipts are visible in either photo.

claims.evidence: No controller is shown in the photos.
The consoles in photos 0 and 1 appear dusty and heavily smudged.
The warranty seal on the rear of the console is not shown.
No controllers are shown in the photos.
The receipt is not shown in the photos.

risks.risk: The controller may be missing, damaged, or a third-party replica.
risks.proof: Clear photos of the front and back of the controller.

risks.risk: The console may have been opened for repair despite claims.
risks.proof: Photo of the intact warranty seal over the screw holes on the back.

risks.risk: The disc drive may be faulty.

proof_requests: Photo of the controller(s) mentioned in the text.
Photo of the back of the console showing the warranty seal and ports.
Photo of the UK receipt mentioned.
Video of the console turned on and running a game.
response.reason: The listing lacks photos of the controller and receipt mentioned in the text. Additionally, the 'never opened' claim cannot be verified without a shot of the warranty seal, and the presence of two different console models in the photos creates ambiguity about which unit is being sold.
